title: Introduce jurisdictional claim normalizer and KMS consent multiplexer
author: Aisha Malik
description: Motivation: customers operating across multiple jurisdictions send heterogeneous region claims and rely on tenant-level KMS consent. This PR implements a rules based claim normalizer plus a consent multiplexer that chooses an authorized KMS provider per effective tenant region, addressing mismatches between operator assertions and downstream key policies while producing richer audit metadata. What changed: 1) services/claim-normalizer service that canonicalizes incoming location claims, supports fuzzy mapping tables and tenant overrides, and emits canonical_region into request context. 2) pkg/kms/consent_mux that evaluates tenant consent profiles, KMS provider allowlists, and per-request residency constraints to select a provider or return a deterministic denial. 3) Integration with policy compiler so RBACv2 decision engine receives normalized claims for accurate policy evaluation and logging. 4) Audit enrichment middleware that stamps canonical_region, kms_provider_hint, and consent_verification into sealed-audit headers. 5) Backfill script and a canary rollout plan behind feature flag rbac.jurisdictional_normalizer. Rollout and safety: feature is gated under opt-in flag, default behavior preserves prior claim passthrough. Canary strategy described in the PR checklist below. Testing: unit tests for normalization rules and mux decision matrix, integration tests exercising policy compiler + KMS selection against mocked provider endpoints, and end-to-end smoke in staging. Backwards compatibility: no public API surface change; operator-managed mappings are additive. Operational notes: added alerts for decision latency and consent cache miss rate, metric labels for canonical_region. References: ENG-3321 for rule set design and SEC-89 for threat model. Checklist: - add service scaffold and tests - wire claim output into request context - integrate with RBACv2 decision path - audit header enrichment - add canary config and backfill script - docs and release notes
